subject.title: refactor(qa): migrate Matrix scenarios into QA Lab

question: Should the production Gateway admission change and additive QA runner lifecycle contract land inside this Matrix QA migration, or should the Gateway fix be split into a focused prerequisite before authorizing the dependency graph?
rationale: The QA migration appears correct, but repository policy treats Gateway lifecycle behavior, Plugin SDK surfaces, and dependency ownership as separate compatibility-sensitive decisions that automated review cannot accept on maintainer intent alone.

options.title: Split Gateway prerequisite
options.body: Move the generic Gateway admission helper and restart call-site changes into a focused prerequisite PR, then rebase this QA migration and authorize its dependency graph.

options.title: Approve combined scope
options.body: Keep the changes together after explicitly accepting the production lifecycle and Plugin SDK surface, with focused Gateway restart proof and exact-head dependency authorization.

options.title: Pause the stack
options.body: Leave this PR open until the remaining Matrix QA stack and long-term qa-matrix removal plan are ready for one coordinated owner review.

recommendation.title: Split Gateway prerequisite
recommendation.body: Move the generic Gateway admission helper and restart call-site changes into a focused prerequisite PR, then rebase this QA migration and authorize its dependency graph.

likelyOwner.reason: This person owns the current four-PR Matrix QA migration stack and is best positioned to explain whether the Gateway behavior is an essential prerequisite or separable repair.
